name: Phobos
title: Phobos: a multi-system emulator for Android handhelds and desktop
description: Phobos is a multi-system emulator built on ares, with a PSP core built from scratch. It's an app for Android ARM64 handhelds, made for controllers, plus a desktop program for Linux, Windows and macOS.
tagline: A multi-system emulator built on ares.
hero_pill: New in 2.0: a PSP core built from scratch
lead_md: An Android app made for handhelds and controllers, plus a desktop program for Linux, Windows and macOS. 34 systems, including the PSP, whose core is built from scratch.

what.title: 34 systems, made for handhelds
paras_md: Phobos is built on [ares](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares), an emulator that puts accuracy first. It keeps ares's cores and adds what a handheld needs, like fast ARM64 paths, Vulkan, custom GPU drivers and a UI you drive with a controller.
Phobos's own code is free software under the GNU GPL, version 3 or later.

platforms.name: Android
platforms.detail: Modern build for ARMv8.2-A with FP16 and dot product, Legacy for any 64-bit ARM device. Android 8.0 or newer.

platforms.name: Linux
platforms.detail: An AppImage, plus a zsync file for smaller updates.

platforms.name: Windows
platforms.detail: Phobos.exe in a zip, for 64-bit Windows.

platforms.name: macOS
platforms.detail: A universal app, with MoltenVK bundled for Vulkan.

what.platforms_note_md: Tagged releases since v2.0.0 have all four. Nightly builds are Android only.

systems_intro_md: Here's where each of the app's 34 systems stands. Arcade has two rows, one for each board.
made_md: I build Phobos with AI coding agents and steer what they work on. Since September, an independent reviewer checks every change before it merges, and speed and accuracy claims come from measurements on my Retroid Pocket 6 and PSP-1000.
disclaimer_md: Phobos comes with no games. Use dumps of games you own. Systems that need a BIOS beyond the firmware ares ships (see [LICENSE](https://github.com/pwnedbygary/phobos/blob/master/LICENSE)) take one dumped from your own hardware. devlog_note_md: Work went straight to master before 24 September 2026, so the log starts there. The PSP core's stack, about 100 pull requests numbered between #100 and #207, reached master together through #208, which is why GitHub shows most of them as [closed](https://github.com/pwnedbygary/phobos/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aclosed). Five show here with the dates they merged into other branches. They're #154, #158, #165 and #179 in the PSP stack, and #275, which reached master through #281.
screens_note_md: Every picture and clip here comes straight from Phobos, running on Linux or on my Retroid Pocket 6.
